verses.text: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” says Yahweh.

Therefore Yahweh, the God of Israel, says against the shepherds who feed my people: “You have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them; behold, I will visit on you the evil of your doings,” says Yahweh.
“I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all the countries where I have driven them, and will bring them again to their folds; and they shall be fruitful and multiply.
I will set up shepherds over them, who shall feed them; and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall any be lacking,” says Yahweh.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will raise to David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king and deal wisely, and shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely. This is his name by which he shall be called: Yahweh our righteousness.
“Therefore behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that they shall no more say, ‘As Yahweh lives, who brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;’

but, ‘As Yahweh lives, who brought up and who led the offspring  of the house of Israel out of the north country, and from all the countries where I had driven them.’ Then they will dwell in their own land.”
Concerning the prophets: My heart within me is broken. All my bones shake. I am like a drunken man, and like a man whom wine has overcome, because of Yahweh, and because of his holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers; for because of the curse the land mourns. The pastures of the wilderness are dried up. Their course is evil, and their might is not right;
for both prophet and priest are profane; yes, in my house I have found their wickedness,” says Yahweh.
Therefore their way shall be to them as slippery places in the darkness. They shall be driven on, and fall therein; for I will bring evil on them, even the year of their visitation,” says Yahweh.
“I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria. They prophesied by Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.

In the prophets of Jerusalem also I have seen a horrible thing: they commit adultery, and walk in lies. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one returns from his wickedness. They have all become to me as Sodom, and its inhabitants as Gomorrah.”

Therefore Yahweh of Armies says concerning the prophets: “Behold, I will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink the water of gall; for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has gone out into all the land.”
Yahweh of Armies says, “Don’t listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They teach you vanity. They speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of Yahweh.
They say continually to those who despise me, ‘Yahweh has said, “You shall have peace;”’ and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart they say, ‘No evil shall come on you.’
For who has stood in the council of Yahweh, that he should perceive and hear his word? Who has listend to my word, and heard it?
Behold, Yahweh’s storm, his wrath, has gone out. Yes, a whirling storm. It shall burst on the head of the wicked.
Yahweh’s anger shall not return, until he has executed, and until he has performed the intents of his heart. In the latter days, you will understand it perfectly.
I didn’t send these prophets, yet they ran. I didn’t speak to them, yet they prophesied.
But if they had stood in my council, then they would have caused my people to hear my words, and would have turned them from their evil way, and from the evil of their doings.
“Am I a God at hand,” says Yahweh, “and not a God afar off?
Can anyone hide himself in secret places so that I can’t see him?” says Yahweh. “Don’t I fill heaven and earth?” says Yahweh.
“I have heard what the prophets have said, who prophesy lies in my name, saying, ‘I had a dream! I had a dream!’
How long shall this be in the heart of the prophets who prophesy lies, even the prophets of the deceit of their own heart?
They intend to cause my people to forget my name by their dreams which they each tell his neighbor, as their fathers forgot my name because of Baal.
The prophet who has a dream, let him tell a dream; and he who has my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the straw to the wheat?” says Yahweh.
“Isn’t my word like fire?” says Yahweh; “and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?
“Therefore behold, I am against the prophets,” says Yahweh, “who each steal my words from his neighbor.
Behold, I am against the prophets,” says Yahweh, “who use their tongues, and say, ‘He says.’

Behold, I am against those who prophesy lying dreams,” says Yahweh, “who tell them, and cause my people to err by their lies, and by their vain boasting; yet I didn’t send them, nor command them; neither do they profit this people at all,” says Yahweh.
“When this people, or the prophet, or a priest, shall ask you, saying, ‘What is the message from Yahweh?’ Then you shall tell them, ‘“What message? I will cast you off,” says Yahweh.’
As for the prophet, and the priest, and the people, who say, ‘The message from Yahweh,’ I will even punish that man and his household.
You shall say everyone to his neighbor, and everyone to his brother, ‘What has Yahweh answered?’ and, ‘What has Yahweh spoken?’
You shall mention the message from Yahweh no more: for every man’s own word has become his message; for you have perverted the words of the living God, of Yahweh of Armies, our God.
You shall say to the prophet, ‘What has Yahweh answered you?’ and, ‘What has Yahweh spoken?’
Although you say, ‘The message from Yahweh;’ therefore Yahweh says: ‘Because you say this word, “The message from Yahweh,” and I have sent to you, telling you not to say, “The message from Yahweh;”
therefore, behold, I will utterly forget you, and I will cast you off, and the city that I gave to you and to your fathers, away from my presence.
I will bring an everlasting reproach on you, and a perpetual shame, which shall not be forgotten.’”

footnotes.content: The Lord's voice carries pain for the scattered ones. Woe falls on those entrusted with care who instead leave the flock defenseless. Even the sternest judgment begins with a broken heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The shepherds have scattered the flock and abandoned them—no visitation, no remedy. Yet the Lord's judgment is not bare wrath; He promises to call leaders to account, to set things right Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From every corner where exile has driven them, the Lord gathers them back. Fruitfulness waiting in the midst of loss—He sees where His own are and draws them home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: New shepherds will feed them, faithful ones who know the Shepherd's heart. No more fear, no more lack—this is what comes when the Lord Himself takes the flock into His care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A righteous Branch from David's line—the prophets knew Him by this name long before He came. He will reign with wisdom, executing justice and righteousness where shepherds had only scattered the flock.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In His days, Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. His name calls out what He is to us: Yahweh our righteousness. No performance required—His justice covers all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The old story of Egypt will give way to a greater one. The Lord prepares a new testimony so mighty that it will eclipse even the Exodus they've sung of for generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the north country and every land of captivity, the Lord brings them home by His own hand. They will dwell in their own land again—not by return alone, but by His leading every step.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah's heart breaks within him—he feels the weight of false prophecy, the desecration of the Lord's words. He trembles because he knows the holiness being trampled, the trust being shattered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land itself suffers under the curse of broken oaths and unfaithfulness. When leaders live in lies, even the earth mourns; the pastures dry up—truth and fruitfulness are bound together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Prophet and priest alike have become profane—defenders of faith corrupted from within. The Lord sees wickedness in His own house, not hidden but openly lodged there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their way becomes treacherous—slippery ground in darkness, no footing secure. They will be driven and fall into the very pit of their own making, for judgment is coming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophets of Samaria spoke by Baal, leading Israel into error. A name that recalls the northern kingdom's long idolatry—the pattern repeats, and Jerusalem now walks the same ruinous path.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem's prophets commit adultery and walk in lies, emboldening the wicked to remain as they are. They have become like Sodom and Gomorrah—the reference chills us with what that means.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wormwood and gall—bitterness upon bitterness. The Lord will feed them with the fruit of their deception, and from Jerusalem's ungodly prophets, corruption spreads through all the land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do not listen. Simple instruction, urgent warning. These prophets teach only what their own hearts have invented, not what the Lord has spoken—vanity wrapped in prophetic robes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "You shall have peace"—the lie that flatters and deceives most easily. No evil will come, they promise the stubborn-hearted, offering false peace when only repentance brings the real thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Has anyone stood in the Lord's council? Has anyone heard His word and truly listened? The question cuts to the heart: these prophets have not. They speak what was never given to them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord's storm gathers and breaks upon the wicked. It is not random chaos but the directed wrath of a just God, whose anger moves with intention toward those who have hardened themselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The anger will not turn back until the Lord has completed His purposes. Someday, they will understand—in the latter days, the meaning will be clear, and they will see that judgment was right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I did not send them. I did not speak to them. Yet they ran with their prophesying as though called. No commission, no word—only the running of their own ambition.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Had they truly stood in His council, they would have turned the people from evil, back toward righteousness. Instead, they strengthen the stubborn—a tragedy of misdirected influence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord is near and far—present in the intimate moment, sovereign over the distant future. He is not confined to one place or one way of knowing; He is fully what they deny.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No secret place hides anyone from Him. Heaven and earth are full of His presence—He sees all, knows all. The prophets' hiding and deception are known in the fullness of His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I had a dream, I had a dream—the repeated refrain of self-deceived prophets. They have heard the Lord's voice in their own sleeping minds, mistaking the dream for the word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How long will the lie persist in their hearts? These are not occasional errors but prophets of deceit, whose very hearts are the fountain of lies—a hardness that will not relent.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: By their dreams they intend to make the people forget the Name. As the fathers forgot before them, turning to Baal, so now a new generation is led astray—the same seduction, the same loss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let the prophet speak his dream as a dream; let the one who has His word speak it faithfully, truly. Straw and wheat—they look alike on the surface, but the difference is everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord's word is fire and hammer—transforming, breaking, reshaping whatever it touches. Not decoration, not comfort only, but power that accomplishes what it is sent to do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord stands against these prophets who steal His words from one another, passing along borrowed speech as though it were revelation. They pilfer from each other and call it prophecy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Against those who use their tongues to declare falsely, 'He says'—the formula of authority that masks the absence of it. They have learned the language of the word but betrayed its substance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Against the prophets of lying dreams who cause the people to err by lies and boasting, claiming they were sent when they were not. They profit nothing for the people—only harm, only a turning away from truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When they ask what message comes from the Lord, the answer is stark: I will cast you off. No word for them but rejection, for they have long rejected the truth He offered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Prophet, priest, people—all who claim the message from the Lord will face His judgment. The very words that should humble them before Him have become a badge of presumption.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let each ask his neighbor and brother, What has the Lord answered? What has He spoken? The search will uncover the emptiness—no word, no answer, only the echo of their own voices.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mention 'the message from the Lord' no more—for now every man's word has become his message. They have perverted the words of the living God, exchanging His truth for their own invention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ask the prophet what the Lord answered him, what He has spoken. The question itself becomes an indictment—for they have no true answer, only the silence of a word never given.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Because you claim the message from the Lord while I have sent word forbidding you to say it, this presumption will cost you. The Lord forbade, yet they continue—adding transgression to rebellion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will utterly forget you and cast you off, you and the city I gave your fathers. The land He provided becomes the judgment He executes—removed from His presence, abandoned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An everlasting reproach and perpetual shame—the weight of this judgment echoes through the ages. Looking back from our own time, we see how kingdoms that rejected the Lord's word fell into obscurity, while those who turned to Him endured. As of 2026-10, the pattern remains: rejection brings forgetting, return brings remembrance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
